question: When SQLite has no subagent rows, runs.json exists, and no trustworthy migration receipt establishes provenance, should Doctor preserve and warn rather than automatically importing the file?
rationale: Source inspection cannot determine whether such a file contains legitimate unimported state or stale state whose rows were intentionally removed; either automatic choice can cause session-state harm.

options.title: Preserve and warn
options.body: Keep the source untouched, avoid resurrection, and provide an explicit Doctor recovery action for operators who confirm the file is authoritative.

options.title: Automatically import
options.body: Prioritize recovery of possible legacy-only runs, accepting that a stale source can recreate intentionally removed registry state.

options.title: Pause the migration
options.body: Do not land the ownership change until a stronger provenance mechanism can distinguish legitimate legacy state from stale sources.

recommendation.title: Preserve and warn
recommendation.body: Keep the source untouched, avoid resurrection, and provide an explicit Doctor recovery action for operators who confirm the file is authoritative.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns closely related SQLite migration provenance and interrupted-recovery contracts.
